conventions.convention: Energies are real-valued and measurable; normalization is defined only for parameters satisfying 0 < Zθ < ∞, relative to the specified reference measure.
The data score is ∇log p on {p > 0} and zero on {p = 0}; the model score is −∇Eθ. Divergence uses locally integrable weak-derivative representatives.
Score matching assumes Countable Choice and finite p-integrals of the squared data score, squared model score and absolute weak divergence; it assumes no pointwise boundary limit at infinity.

CD-k starts each reconstruction chain from the data law, uses k ≥ 1 transitions, and updates θ ← θ − η ĝk. Its population direction is the data energy-gradient mean minus the reconstruction energy-gradient mean.

Finite-state probability vectors are row vectors, qk,θ = q0 Kθ^k, and Kθ^0 = I. The transition matrix is strictly positive; q0 may have zero coordinates. KL uses natural logarithms and zero-mass terms contribute zero.

The scalar CD objective retains parameter dependence through the reconstruction law; the stop-gradient update omits it and is not asserted to equal either the exact CD gradient or the likelihood gradient.

load_bearing.statement: For a measure space (X, A, μ) and measurable real energies Eθ, Zθ := ∫ exp(−Eθ) dμ, Θμ := {θ : 0 < Zθ < ∞}, and Pθ(A) := Zθ⁻¹ ∫A exp(−Eθ) dμ for θ ∈ Θμ.

For an admissible energy model, a data probability law Q0 and an invariant probability kernel Kθ, define Qj+1,θ(A) = ∫ Kθ(x,A) Qj,θ(dx). For k ≥ 1 and m ≥ 1, draw independent data starts and conditionally independent k-transition reconstructions, form ĝk = m⁻¹ Σi(∇θEθ(xi) − ∇θEθ(xi,k)), and update θ ← θ − ηĝk. When the gradients are integrable under Q0 and Qk,θ, the population direction is their corresponding difference of integrals.

On a finite nonempty state space, with open parameter domain, continuously coordinate-differentiable energies and strictly positive stochastic transition entries, invariant model law pθ, fixed probability vector q0 and k ≥ 1, ∂jL = Σx q0(x)∂jEθ(x) − Σx pθ(x)∂jEθ(x), while ∂jCDk = Σx q0(x)∂jEθ(x) − Σx qk,θ(x)∂jEθ(x) − Σx ∂jqk,θ(x) log(qk,θ(x)/pθ(x)), where ∂jqk,θ = Σs=0,…,k−1 q0Kθ^s(∂jKθ)Kθ^(k−1−s).
For every measure space (X, A, μ), measurable real energy Eθ, and parameter θ with 0 < Zθ := ∫ exp(−Eθ) dμ < ∞, the normalized measure Pθ(A) := Zθ⁻¹ ∫A exp(−Eθ) dμ is a probability measure on (X, A).
